title: Inflammatory memory primes the intestine for enhanced regenerative potential [multiome 1]
overall_design: Lgr5-GFP-IRES-CreERT2:Rosa26-tdTomato mice were treated with 4-hydroxytamoxifen to permanently label Lgr5⁺ intestinal stem cells and their progeny. One day later, mice were subjected to irradiation. After 21 days, tdTomato⁺ epithelial cells were isolated by flow cytometry from irradiated and control mice. Cells were analyzed using 10x Genomics single-cell multiome sequencing (scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq).

title: Inflammatory memory primes the intestine for enhanced regenerative potential [multiome 2]
overall_design: Krt20CreERT2:Rosa26-tdTomato mice were injected with 4-hydroxytamoxifen to induce permanent labeling of Krt20⁺ differentiated epithelial cells, located in the villi and upper crypt regions. Then, mice were subjected to abdominal irradiation. In non-irradiated controls, labeled cells were lost within a few days due to normal epithelial turnover. In contrast, irradiated mice showed persistence of tdTomato⁺ cells in the crypts 21 days post-injury, indicating dedifferentiation and repopulation of the ISC compartment. tdTomato⁺ cells from irradiated mice and epithelial cells from controls were isolated by flow cytometry and analyzed using 10x Genomics single-cell multiome sequencing (scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq).

title: Inflammatory memory primes the intestine for enhanced regenerative potential [ATAC-seq]
overall_design: To assess the impact of IFNγ signaling on long-term epigenetic remodeling after radiation injury, mice were divided into three groups: unirradiated controls, mice exposed to a single abdominal irradiation dose, and mice irradiated and treated with anti-IFNγ blocking antibody every three days for three weeks post-injury. At 21 days after irradiation, intestinal epithelial cells were isolated by flow cytometry from all groups. Nuclei were extracted and subjected to bulk ATAC-seq to profile genome-wide chromatin accessibility. This design enabled the comparison of chromatin landscapes associated with injury-induced epigenetic memory and the effects of IFNγ inhibition on this process.

title: Transcriptional dynamics in immune population upon irradiation
overall_design: Mice were subjected to abdominal irradiation (14 Gy), and immune cells were isolated at baseline (control), 7 days, 21 days.

title: Transcriptomic dynamic changes upon irradiation and organoid culture on intestinal epithelial cells
overall_design: Mice were subjected to abdominal irradiation (14 Gy), and intestinal epithelial cells were isolated at baseline (control), 7 days, 21 days, and 3 months post-irradiation. RNA extraction was performed at each time point.  In addition, organoid cultures were established from epithelial cells at 21 days post-irradiation and control. After several passages in vitro, RNA was extracted to assess whether irradiation-induced effects were maintained.
